content.text: •inflam → edema · bronchospasm · ↑mucus in bronchioles → ↑airway resistance → resp distress/↑work of breathing
•infants = obligate nasal breathers - nasal passages = 50% of airway resistance
*MC in first 2 mo- 2 yr of life
: premature (<37wk) · ↓breast feeding · <6 mo · smoke exposure · crowded conditions
•Viral Prodrome (fever · URI sx for 1-2 days) → resp distress
•1-3d prodrome mild URI (low-grade fever · rhinorrhea) → cough + resp difficulty
•nasal drainage · intercostal/subcostal retractions · polyphonic wheeze · fine/coarse crackles (rales)
for children <29 wks for first yr of life
•nasal suctioning = 1st step · hydration · parent education/anticipatory guidance
•noninvasive ventilation (nasal CPAP · BiPAP · HFNC) b4 intubation - intubate after failure of suction · O2 · positive pressure
•inflam of epiglottis · aryepiglottic folds · arytenoids · supraglottic tissues - infect or trauma
•Hib classic (gram ⊖ - also meningitis · OM · PNA) · other H. flu · GABHS · S. aureus · S. pneumo - Hib vax ↓incidence
•rapid onset sore throat + fever → can quickly progress to upper airway obstruct
•toxic · ↑fever · drooling prominent · sniffing position · leaning forward · supraclavicular retractions
•lat neck XR when sus (febrile · ill-appearing · drooling +/- stridor)
Maintaining airway most important component of mgnt
•O2 least invasive - rapidly deteriorating: bag-valve-mask · fiberoptic intubation · needle cricothyroidotomy · tracheostomy - temporary until airway expert (anesthesia · ENT · gen surg)
•admit pediatric ICU once airway secure - USU intubated 3-5d
ddx bact tracheitis: bact infect of trach - can be comp of croup - several days viral URI prodrome (cough · fever) → insp & exp stridor → severe
